newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.
newsitem.headline: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.

text.p: Japan's NEC Corp announced on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement to set up a joint venture in China to produce semiconductors.
The project will cost a total of $1 billion, the company said in a statement.

NEC and its Chinese partner, Shanghai Hua Hong, would form the joint venture company in July to design, manufacture and market semiconductors using NEC's latest chip technology, an NEC spokesman said.

He said NEC would contribute 28.6 percent of the venture's $700 million capital and Shanghai Hua Hong the remaining 71.4 percent. The company will be based in Shanghai's Pudong district and the project located in Beijing.
The new plant will start full-scale volume production of dynamic random access memory chips and applied specific integrated circuits in the first half of 1999, he added.

The spokesman said the agreement was a result of NEC's participation in China's five-year plan to develop its semiconductor industry and added that NEC was selected as the exclusive partner for the plan.
